panels.description: Current role of the box. Derived from the dynamic mode=gaming taint (kube-state-metrics) plus node-exporter reachability: 0/2 = ASLEEP (node down), 1 = COMPUTE (awake, no gaming taint), 3 = GAMING (awake, mode=gaming:NoSchedule present). The node sleeps routinely — ASLEEP is the normal idle state, not an outage.

targets.expr: (max(kube_node_spec_taint{node="gpu-node",key="mode",value="gaming"}) or on() vector(0)) * 2 + (max(up{job="node-exporter",instance="172.16.1.220:9100"}) or on() vector(0))

panels.title: Mode

panels.description: Which pod currently holds the GPU. DCGM series carry the namespace/pod labels of the workload occupying the card — this is the one panel where those labels are the point instead of noise. Empty while asleep or when nothing has the GPU allocated.
panels.title: GPU workload

panels.description: Most recent Xid error code reported by DCGM. 79 = "GPU has fallen off the bus" — on this box that was GDDR6X memory-junction heat-soak in the FormD T1, fixed by a bottom intake fan + PTM7950 repad (see docs/lessons/xid79-gddr6x-heat-soak.md). Anything non-zero deserves a look at dmesg. Shows "none" when no Xid metric is present (asleep, or no error since exporter start).
panels.title: Last Xid

panels.description: GPU die (edge) temperature. Water-cooled: sustained 350W tensor compute holds 60-62°C since the 2026-06-08 PTM7950 repad. The GDDR6X junction is NOT observable on consumer Ampere (DCGM_FI_DEV_MEMORY_TEMP reads 0) — die temp alone can look fine while memory heat-soaks.
panels.title: GPU temp

panels.description: Loop water temperature (ASUS EC T_Sensor, asusec temp4). CPU and GPU share one loop and one radiator; the CoolerControl "watercurve" drives the rad fans off this value.
panels.title: Water

panels.description: GPU board power draw. Both modes run -pl 370 (gpu-profile v3.0); sustained training typically sits 300-350W.
panels.title: GPU power

panels.description: Framebuffer used, out of the RTX 3080's 10240 MiB (values are MiB — DCGM reports FB in MiB).
panels.title: VRAM

panels.description: Sleep/wake and mode history over the last 24h (fixed window regardless of dashboard range). Blue = asleep — the controller wakes the box on demand and suspends it when idle, so blue stretches are normal. The query synthesizes 0 while the node is down, so there are no gaps.

targets.expr: (max(kube_node_spec_taint{node="gpu-node",key="mode",value="gaming"}) or on() vector(0)) * 2 + (max(up{job="node-exporter",instance="172.16.1.220:9100"}) or on() vector(0))

panels.title: Awake / mode (24h)

panels.description: Fraction of the selected dashboard range the node was awake (node-exporter target up). ~30% over a typical week — the box sleeps when nothing needs it.
panels.title: Awake % (range)

panels.description: GPU energy over the last 24h from DCGM's cumulative energy counter (mJ → kWh). Approximate: the counter resets on driver reload and the series fragments when the GPU-holding pod changes, so increase() can undercount across those boundaries. Good enough for "what does training cost me".
panels.title: GPU energy (24h)

panels.description: Board power vs the 370W power limit (red line). gpu-profile v3.0 sets -pl 370 in BOTH modes — earlier PL300/PL320 "transient protection" values were chasing a heat-soak problem that turned out to be mechanical. max() across DCGM series because labels fragment when the GPU-holding pod changes.
panels.title: Power draw

panels.description: SM occupancy, memory-bandwidth utilization, and NVENC/NVDEC. In gaming mode NVENC carries the Sunshine HEVC 10-bit stream; in compute mode it should be 0. SM high + MemBW high is the sustained-tensor-compute profile that used to end in Xid 79 before the airflow/repad fixes.
panels.title: Utilization

panels.description: SM and memory clocks. CUDA workloads force P2, which caps the memory clock at 9251 MHz by VBIOS design (P0 would be 9501) — not a bug, and -lmc is accepted-but-ignored. gpu-profile lifts the core boost ceiling to 2160 MHz via -lgc 0,2160; memory OC is impossible headless (needs Xorg/nvidia-settings).
panels.title: Clocks

panels.description: Framebuffer in use, MiB, fixed axis to 10240 (RTX 3080 10GB) so a full card is obvious. Used only — used+free+reserved always sums to 10 GB, so stacking them is wasted ink.
panels.title: VRAM used
Reliability — needs dcgm-exporter 04-custom-counters.yaml applied; those panels show No data until then

panels.description: Xid error codes as reported by DCGM. Event-sparse: flat 0 (or No data while asleep) is the desired state. A 79 here = "GPU has fallen off the bus" — the GDDR6X heat-soak failure mode documented in docs/lessons/xid79-gddr6x-heat-soak.md.
panels.title: Xid errors

panels.description: Raw clock-event (throttle) reason bitmask. Key bits: 0x01 GPU idle, 0x04 SW power cap, 0x08 HW slowdown, 0x20 SW thermal slowdown — THE GDDR6X heat-soak signature on this card (fires at die temp 65-70°C because the invisible memory junction is near its limit), 0x40 HW thermal, 0x80 HW power brake. Custom counter: No data until 04-custom-counters.yaml is applied.
panels.title: Throttle reasons bitmask

panels.description: Time per second spent throttled, by cause (DCGM violation counters are cumulative µs). "Thermal" climbing while GPU die temp looks fine is the memory heat-soak tell. Custom counters: No data until 04-custom-counters.yaml is applied.
panels.title: Throttle time by cause

panels.description: GPU performance state. 0 = P0 (idle/gaming boost), 2 = P2 — the forced state for all CUDA work on consumer Ampere (this is what caps memory at 9251 MHz). Custom counter: No data until 04-custom-counters.yaml is applied.
panels.title: P-state

panels.description: PCIe replay (retry) rate. A low background rate under load is normal for this slot; a sustained jump was one of the red-herring suspects during the Xid 79 hunt — it correlates with load, not with the crashes.
panels.title: PCIe replay rate

panels.description: Everything thermal on one axis. Water = ASUS EC T_Sensor (loop temp; CPU+GPU share one loop/radiator). GPU die from DCGM. nct6775 AUXTIN0/AUXTIN3 (temp3/temp6) are floating inputs reading constant 80-86°C — deliberately excluded, never chart them. The GDDR6X memory junction is NOT measurable on consumer Ampere and can run far hotter than the die (see docs/lessons/xid79-gddr6x-heat-soak.md).
panels.title: Temperatures

panels.description: Radiator fans (nct6798 fan1/fan2, on the water-temp curve), loop pump (AIO_PUMP header, Alphacool DC-LT) and the small VRM heatsink fan. The pump runs at fixed 100% — it should sit flat around 2700 RPM and is never on a curve; a sagging pump line means trouble.
panels.title: Fans & pump RPM

panels.description: PWM duty cycle (raw 0-255 scaled to %). pwm1/pwm2 = rad fans on the CoolerControl watercurve; pwm5 = pump, pinned at 100% (never curved).
panels.title: PWM duty

panels.description: GPU die minus loop water temperature — a proxy for block contact / TIM health. The PTM7950 repad (2026-06-08) brought the loaded delta from 25-45°C down to ~10-13°C. A rising trend at comparable power means the paste/pad is degrading again; dashed line at 20°C as the "go look at it" mark.
panels.title: GPU − water ΔT

panels.description: Overall CPU busy % (1 − idle, averaged over 16 threads). Training dataloaders are usually the only thing that pushes this; both modes pin the performance governor.
panels.title: CPU %

panels.description: Memory in use as % of 32 GiB (1 − MemAvailable/MemTotal).
panels.title: Memory %

panels.description: Load averages. 16 hardware threads, so 16 = fully loaded.
panels.title: Load (1/5/15)

panels.description: enp7s0 (Intel I225-V, 2.5GbE) throughput in bits/s; tx drawn below the axis. Sunshine streaming shows a steady ~50 Mbit/s tx (max_bitrate 50000).
panels.title: Network enp7s0

panels.description: Filesystem usage on the two data partitions of the single 1TB NVMe (p3 = / 150G, p4 = /home, which holds models/datasets and the Steam library).
panels.title: Disk used %

panels.description: Fraction of time nvme0n1 (Crucial P5 Plus) spent with I/O in flight. Sustained 100% during training usually means the dataloader is disk-bound.
panels.title: Disk IO util %
